note: A motor can be longer than its mount tube. The "Max motor length" estimate used to stop at the front of the motor mount tube, which is not what stops a motor - the mount is a framework for the motor to sit in. It now walks forward out of the mount and up the stage to the first real obstruction: an engine block or bulkhead (in a dual-deploy rocket, the ebay's aft bulkhead), the back of the nose cone, or a transition that narrows. It never crosses a stage boundary. Read the "Room for ..." line, which names what stopped it: a design that models nothing inside its airframe will now measure most of that airframe and say it stopped at the nose cone, which is the cue to model your ebay bulkhead. The floating stats gadget also starts open again rather than folded.
